Round 152 is planned and dispatched as `CONTINUE`. It's a small round that closes V-2a (Studio fonts) so that rounds 151 and 152 can be published together. I didn't touch any app source; `git status` still shows A's 9 round-151 paths with their end hashes.

**What happened in round 151:** C failed it, with only Low findings. Browser checks ran for real (`browserVerified` and `realVerified` both true) and 13 rows passed in Chromium. Gate 151 was skipped, so nothing was published. The baseline for round 152 is therefore HEAD `e94ae88` plus A's unpublished round-151 work (8 changed files and 1 new file). That work is preserved and nobody may revert it.

**My rulings (D-29z117):**
- **C-R151-1:** the shortcut-hint line got 119 px narrower, which broke the "panels stay within ±1 px" rule. C's measuring tool tags that line as a panel, but its box is just its own text width, so it's text whose width changed. I changed the rule to count it as text; every other layout rule stays. Fixing its width instead would be a layout change the user hasn't approved.
- **C-R151-2:** the " · " separators look cramped in the new font: 5 px at 12 px, against 9 px in Inter. There's no fix inside the approved typography, which allows only font, weight and letter-spacing. I moved it to `deferred_low_polish` and recorded it as a question for the user with three measured options:
  - accept it;
  - add `word-spacing: 0.12em`, which brings the gap to about 8.8 px with no vertical moves but leaves the dot itself 1 px wide;
  - use a different separator character, which changes text in 94 lines.

  It still has to be fixed or accepted before final sign-off.
- **C-R151-3:** the "∞" in "−∞" falls back to another monospace font. None of Google's IBM Plex Mono files include that character, and self-hosting fonts isn't allowed by the spec. Moved to `deferred_low_polish`.

Both rulings that change what counts as passing (the hint ruling and the earlier ≤ ~9 px horizontal-shift ruling) are flagged in `feature-status.md` so the user can veto them.

My round-151 task had said a Low caused by the round gets a fix-up, not a deferral. The user's 2026-10-23 rule says new Lows during the visual stage are deferred, so I followed that and wrote down the conflict in `b-round-151.md`.

**Round 152 task:**
- **A** owns 2 files; the other 969 are frozen:
  - doc 123: add the round-151 results, the rulings and the user question;
  - one line in the theme test, so it checks the exact number of pan-reset buttons (I expect 3) instead of "more than 0".

  A runs one mutation check (m133). If the count isn't 3, A writes the real number and the reason.
- **C**, in real Chromium at 1440×900 and 1280×720:
  - re-runs the layout check under the corrected rule, recording the tool change;
  - checks that the Store pages still download none of the Studio font files, even after hovering the header link (a prefetch of the font stylesheet is allowed);
  - repeats the source-scope, font spot, function smoke, auth and network checks.

**Coming next:** the regression round is due from 2026-10-27, so if round 153 is planned then, the regression goes first. After that comes V-2b, the second typography stage. A quick check I ran found that the only Studio text at 16 px or larger is the transport time readout and one icon. The display serif may therefore have nothing to apply to without enlarging text, which would need the user's approval. Neither user decision file exists yet. The architecture checkpoint request is still pending with you and doesn't block anything. Rounds 151 and 152 can only be committed after C passes round 152.

I archived the round-151 task unchanged as `tasks/round-151.md` and kept "before" copies of the backlog, board, plan and old `b-next.json` in `b-round-151/`. The advisor was available and I used it twice, before writing and before finishing; its three fixes to the task are applied.

Everything is in `/home/runner/czaba-project/tmp/studio-real-loop/`:
- current-task.md
